page: Vultr vx1-g-4c-16g-240s is a general-purpose virtual server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, built on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 240 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-threaded performance alongside average multi-threaded and memory bandwidth capabilities. The server achieves top-tier results in stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded operations like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. However, multi-threaded scaling is a notable bottleneck, with geekbench multi-core scores and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falling into the weak category. Memory bandwidth remains average, registering 440.06 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 70.96 GB/sec for uncached large blocks.

This hardware profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that prioritize single-core throughput over massive parallelization. It is well-suited for general-purpose tasks, static web serving, text processing, and lightweight database operations. It can handle small-scale LLM inference, though performance drops significantly on medium 7B models.
description: The Vultr vx1-g-4c-16g-240s is a general-purpose virtual server from the VX1 Cloud Compute family. Powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor, it offers 4 dedicated vCPUs, 16.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 240 GB NVMe SSD. Benchmarks show top-tier single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and text processing. However, multi-core scaling is weaker, as evidenced by lower multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench multi-core scores. Memory bandwidth and database operations perform at average levels. This server is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that rely on single-threaded efficiency, such as static web serving, text processing, and lightweight database tasks, rather than highly parallelized compute jobs. The system also includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and supports virtualization via AMD SVM.
